segments: and he lessened his submission to the Sultan,
and from the booty he acquired,
he sent nothing according to custom.
And because of this, that Sultan, Ghiyath al-Din Muhammad, took offense at him,
and he sent against him Amir Mawdud with other amirs and a large army (and many forces) in the year 502
502 of the Arabs.
And that Jawali, when he heard that they were coming against him,
fortified Mosul,
and he left in it his wife, who was the sister of Bursuq,
one of the amirs who had come against Mosul.
And he stationed fighters on the wall,
and he left and went out as if to bring other people to his aid,
and so that he would not be shut up in the city.
And he took out with him also Baldwin, the Frankish Count,
who had been held captive with him in Mosul.
And he assessed
upon him seventy thousand dinars,
and that he should set free the Arab captives who were with him,
and whenever necessity called,
he should come with a force of the Franks to his aid.
And he sent him to Qal'at Ja'bar,
that he might be there until he fulfilled his promises.
Now that Baldwin, when he went,
sent and brought Joscelin, his sister's son,
and placed him as a hostage in his stead,
and he himself went to prepare the gold.
Now that wife of Jawali who had been left behind in Mosul
began to mistreat the people of Mosul,
and she oppressed them with heavy taxes.
And because of this, some of the city's inhabitants, craftsmen who worked in plaster, seized control of one of the towers,
and they shouted:
"Long live the Great Sultan, Muhammad Ghiyath al-Din!"
And thus Amir Mawdud and those with him entered,
and they took possession of Mosul.
And the wife of Jawali went out to her brother Bursuq.
Jawali, however, went to Ilghazi, the lord of Nisibis and of Mardin,
while he was in 'Araban, a village on the Khabur.
And he strove hard to come to an agreement with him,
but Ilghazi was not willing,
but left him and went up to the fortress of Mardin.
And Jawali came against Rahba,
and he fought against it for seventy days.
And he sent and brought Joscelin from Qal'at Ja'bar,
and clothed him in royal garments,
and gave him the horse on which he had been riding,
and sent him to Baldwin, his kinsman,
that he might hasten in preparing the gold
and the release of the captives.
